milestone.title: mp autopilot cycle flow + decision matrix + topology tightening

intent.outcome: The orchestrator drives a milestone through orchestrator→runner→orchestrator→reviewer→orchestrator cycle flow, applies the documented decision matrix (per-cycle governance: 2 default, soft cap 3, hard limit 4; cycle-next / ship-with-backlog / escalate), and respects the topology-mode tightening (3-pane = full matrix; 2-pane = no ship-with-backlog; 1-pane = no external review).

problem.description: The project log's R2/R3/R11 captured hard requirements (cycle caps, decision matrix, reviewer activation by orchestrator prompt) that drove M200/M201/M202/M203 to completion in 3-4 cycles each, with a documented soft cap hit twice (M200, M201). The new autopilot system needs the cycle machinery as code, not as a procedure the agent follows: a state machine that runs the cycle, applies the matrix after each reviewer verdict, and tightens itself based on topology. Without this, the orchestrator has no formal cycle governance and either never progresses or ships-with-too-many-bugs.

in_scope: Cycle-flow state machine in `crates/mp/src/autopilot/cycle.rs`: states `Dispatching`, `WaitingRunner`, `Reviewing`, `Deciding`, `AwaitingUser`; transitions driven by lane notifications (C1) and verifier verdicts (C2). One full cycle is `Dispatching → WaitingRunner → Reviewing → Deciding → (cycle-next → Dispatching | ship | escalate).`

Decision matrix as a pure function in `crates/mp/src/autopilot/decision.rs`: `decide_after_review(verdict: ReviewReport, cycle: u8) -> CycleDecision { CycleNext, ShipWithBacklog, Escalate }`. Inputs: severity counts, drift ratio, current cycle number. Documented thresholds per the log's R3.
Cycle-cap enforcement: default 2 cycles, soft cap 3 (tightened reviewer prompt — `blockers only` — kicks in at cycle 2), hard limit 4 (forces `Escalate` regardless of verdict).

Topology-mode tightening consumes B1's `topology_tightening(topology) -> MatrixMode` (`FullMatrix` / `NoShipWithBacklog` / `NoExternalReview`) and applies it: 2-pane removes the `ShipWithBacklog` arm; 1-pane skips `Reviewing` entirely and ships via a typed `SingleAgentShip` arm.

Reviewer activation by orchestrator prompt (per R11): the cycle-flow state machine includes a `DispatchReviewer` transition that sends a fixed-shape `review_request` shell command to the reviewer pane carrying the milestone id, cycle number, and evidence refs.
out_of_scope: The lane-notify wire format — that's C1.
The role config and topology declaration — that's B1.

acceptance_criteria.description: The cycle-flow state machine runs through one full cycle (Dispatching → WaitingRunner → Reviewing → Deciding → cycle-next → Dispatching) for an in-test milestone with stubbed TUI-relay events (lane state changes surfaced via session.json writes, then relayed to the orchestrator by the TUI per E's mediator role).
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; when the matching test fixture exists, this verification is replaced with a per-AC `cargo nextest run -p <crate> --test <name> --no-fail-fast` command.

acceptance_criteria.description: The decision matrix returns the documented outcome for representative inputs: `high_severity + cycle=1 → CycleNext`; `low_count<=2 + cycle=2 → ShipWithBacklog` (verified by an end-state fixture that asserts the milestone ends as `ship-with-backlog` in reviews.json, not just that the matrix returns the enum); `cycle=4 → Escalate`. Each arm is locked by an explicit test fixture.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; when the matching test fixture exists, this verification is replaced with a per-AC `cargo nextest run -p <crate> --test <name> --no-fail-fast` command.

acceptance_criteria.description: Topology-mode tightening: 2-pane returns `NoShipWithBacklog` (low-severity findings force `CycleNext` instead of `ShipWithBacklog`); 1-pane returns `NoExternalReview` (the `Reviewing` state is skipped and the matrix has no `Reviewer` input).
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; verifier allows manual ACs in draft state. Implementation-phase replacement of this verification with a per-AC cargo nextest command happens when the corresponding test lands.

acceptance_criteria.description: Cycle-cap enforcement: synthetic 4-cycle milestone reaches `Escalate` even if all prior verdicts were `Pass`. Soft-cap kicks in at cycle 2 (tightened-reviewer-prompt flag). When cycle 4's verifier reports `cycle-next` (continuation-impossible), the cycle-flow escalates immediately to user with the typed `CycleCapExhausted` event — not `cycle-next`. This sub-case was untested in M200 (which hit cycle 4 but the review passed); lock it as an explicit test fixture.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; when the matching test fixture exists, this verification is replaced with a per-AC `cargo nextest run -p <crate> --test <name> --no-fail-fast` command.

acceptance_criteria.description: Reviewer activation: `DispatchReviewer` transition sends a `herdr agent prompt <reviewer-pane-id> "..."` shell command with the documented `review_request` payload (milestone id, cycle number, evidence refs); the rendered command is auditable.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; verifier allows manual ACs in draft state. Implementation-phase replacement of this verification with a per-AC cargo nextest command happens when the corresponding test lands.

acceptance_criteria.description: Stale-state timeout: if the lane's state in session.json.roles.<role>.state has not changed within `autopilot.stale_state_secs` seconds while the cycle-flow expects it to (e.g., runner should transition to `Done` after Working), the cycle-flow raises a typed `StaleStateTimeout` event and the topology-aware escalation in C2 routes it (3-pane: resend + log; 2-pane: escalate to user; 1-pane: always escalate).
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; when the matching test fixture exists, this verification is replaced with a per-AC `cargo nextest run -p <crate> --test <name> --no-fail-fast` command.

acceptance_criteria.description: predict_next_action(cycle_state, recent_events) -> NextAction is a pure function with at least 6 named outcomes (DispatchRunner, DispatchReviewer, AwaitRunner, AwaitReviewer, ApplyMatrix, EscalateUser). Returns one of these based on the cycle state machine's current position and last TUI-relay event. The TUI's per-milestone detail view consumes this directly so users can see 'what's next' for each queued milestone.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — implementation produces the documented behavior; when the matching test fixture exists, this verification is replaced with a per-AC `cargo nextest run -p <crate> --test <name> --no-fail-fast` command.

design_decisions.choice: Pure state machine (states + transitions as data); the dispatcher function consumes events and returns next state + side-effects.
design_decisions.rationale: Same shape as M190's sequencer; tests are deterministic by feeding event sequences.

design_decisions.choice: Tightened prompt (cycle 2 onward: 'blockers only') is a flag passed to the reviewer-activation template; reviewers see `mode=blockers-only` in their prompt.
design_decisions.rationale: Per the log: tightening at cycle 2 catches drift faster than tightening at cycle 3 (M201's experience).

design_decisions.choice: 1-pane topology's `Deciding` state consumes the orchestrator's self-review verdict (no separate reviewer); the matrix degenerates to `Ship (no verification)` since the agent has already done both the work and the review.
design_decisions.rationale: This is the topology tightening's terminal case; restricts 1-pane to tracks and trivial fixes (B1 already documents this).

steps.action: Implement predict_next_action in crates/mp/src/autopilot/cycle.rs as a pure function. Inputs: the cycle-flow state's current position (e.g., Dispatching, WaitingRunner, Reviewing, Deciding, AwaitingUser) and the last N TUI-relay events (lane state changes surfaced via session.json). Output: a typed NextAction enum with at least 6 variants (DispatchRunner, DispatchReviewer, AwaitRunner, AwaitReviewer, ApplyMatrix, EscalateUser). Tested against hand-built (state, events) -> expected_outcome fixtures covering each variant plus topology-aware escalation.
